description: The 'Orchestrator ruling on the census mismatch (recorded run 4, attempt 2, 2026-08-11)' section resolves a genuine 10-inventory disposition disagreement over one file (`.agents/skills/diagnosing-bugs/scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh`: this run's own inventory.md calls it `decompose`, run 3's inventory calls it `helper-evidence`) by directly citing the reference corpus's own answer: "ruled in run 3's favor because run 3 matches the FROZEN reference corpus (`reference-corpus/source-inventory.md` line 64: helper-evidence, ladder §6.5; its behavior is BU-P2-024, representation "helper", N1 adjudication A11)". This is a hit inside a citation field per the checklist's own taxonomy (Axis 1, blindness boundary) — the run's harvest scope (whether this file is decomposed into behavior units at all) was decided by directly consulting the answer key's own line number, disposition, and adjudication ID, not by this run's own independent judgment. The file's exclusion from the harvested corpus (see AF-0003/AF-0004) is a direct, traceable downstream effect of this contamination. The ledger's own hedge ("This stage's actor did not consult reference-corpus/ ... the ruling ... was supplied pre-adjudicated by the orchestrator, not derived by this stage") does not cure the contamination — the citation and its content are now written into this run's own committed evidence regardless of which actor looked at the excluded directory first, and the ruling was used to decide this run's own generative output.
evidence: 20-harvest/output/partition-ledger.md, section "Orchestrator ruling on the census mismatch", quoting: "is ruled in run 3's favor because run 3 matches the FROZEN reference corpus (`reference-corpus/source-inventory.md` line 64: helper-evidence, ladder §6.5; its behavior is BU-P2-024, representation "helper", N1 adjudication A11)" and the disposition line "`.agents/skills/diagnosing-bugs/scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh` is **not** harvested by this stage". Confirmed via `grep -rn reference-corpus .sergeant/workflows/repo-to-icm/` that this is the only hit inside 00-contract through 70-lint outputs that names specific reference-corpus content (a line number, a disposition, and an adjudication ID) rather than restating the exclusion policy's own wording.

description: 00-contract/output/contract.md §3 explicitly rules this is NOT a measurement run: "this run's task carries no measurement framing and no answer-key directory is present in this worktree, so that clause does not resolve to an actual exclusion here—recorded as a discrepancy worth a downstream reader's attention, not silently reconciled." No stage between 00-contract and 20-harvest revises or overturns that ruling. Yet 20-harvest/output/partition-ledger.md's own census-mismatch ruling treats this explicitly as a graded comparison run: it cites "the FROZEN reference corpus", an "N1 adjudication", and frames the file-level disagreement as needing to be "recorded here only as a generator-vs-reference disposition disagreement for the comparison record" (twice, in the ruling and in the disposition paragraph). This is an internal contradiction the run never surfaces or reconciles: the contract this run is supposed to operate under says there is no reference corpus to be blind to, while the harvest stage's own committed text treats the run as being actively graded against one and pulls content from it accordingly.
evidence: 00-contract/output/contract.md line ~61-65 ("this run's task carries no measurement framing ... recorded as a discrepancy worth a downstream reader's attention, not silently reconciled") versus 20-harvest/output/partition-ledger.md's ruling section ("matches the FROZEN reference corpus", "N1 adjudication A11", "stands recorded here only as a generator-vs-reference disposition disagreement for the comparison record").

description: inventory.md states a `decompose` disposition count of 83 (Disposition counts table, and 83+80+16+0=179 check), including `.agents/skills/diagnosing-bugs/scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh` (partition E row). Recomputing the number of distinct `source.path` values directly from `20-harvest/output/behavior-units.ndjson` (not copied from any other artifact) gives 82, not 83. The one-file gap is exactly the same file the AF-0001 ruling excluded from harvest. inventory.md's own stated decompose count was never revised to reflect that its own file's actual downstream harvest yield is one short of what it claims.
evidence: Recomputed via direct parse of 20-harvest/output/behavior-units.ndjson (1333 records, `len(set(d['source']['path'] for d in records))` = 82). inventory.md "Disposition counts" table states `decompose: 83` and the checksum line "83 + 80 + 16 + 0 = 179. ✓" (10-inventory/output/inventory.md). inventory.md partition E row explicitly lists `scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh` as `D` (decompose).

description: consequence-class-sweep.md is required to have exactly one row per `decompose` file named in inventory.md. It has 82 data rows (82 distinct file paths, no blank cells, no duplicate rows — verified directly), but inventory.md names 83 `decompose` files. The missing row is `.agents/skills/diagnosing-bugs/scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh`, the same file AF-0001/AF-0003 identify as excluded via the reference-corpus-sourced ruling. This is the exact "missing row" condition the checklist names as a finding in its own right, independent of the count mismatch already recorded as AF-0003.
evidence: Recomputed directly: `20-harvest/output/consequence-class-sweep.md` contains 82 data rows (header+separator excluded), 82 distinct first-column file paths, 0 blank cells. `grep -n hitl-loop 20-harvest/output/consequence-class-sweep.md` returns no match. inventory.md's decompose census (83 files, including that path) is the file this sweep is supposed to have one row per.

description: partition-ledger.md shows 21 partitions (P1–P21, all `done`) — this is run 3's own partition scheme, explicitly borrowed ("Scheme provenance (run 4)": harvesting proceeds "by run 3's partition scheme"). This run's own 10-inventory/output/inventory.md instead partitions the same file census into 19 differently-named partitions (A–S, e.g. "A. Coordinator root instructions & toolbelt reference", "B. Installation, environment, and project-config schema", ...). No partition name in partition-ledger.md (P1–P21) appears in inventory.md (A–S), and vice versa — the two files' own partition tables are entirely disjoint in name, count, and order, even though both claim to partition the same decompose-file census for the same run. The ledger explains why (a resumed run reconciling at the file level, not the partition-label level) but the checklist's literal self-consistency check still names this condition as a finding regardless of explanation, since a reader comparing the two artifacts' "partition" columns directly would find no correspondence at all.
evidence: 20-harvest/output/partition-ledger.md's table header lists P1–P21 (e.g. "P1: Root agent policy", "P21: Sergeant-authored operational skills"). 10-inventory/output/inventory.md's "Partition counts" table lists A–S (e.g. "A. Coordinator root instructions & toolbelt reference", "S. Bash version guard (bin/)"). Zero overlap in the two label sets.

description: BU-0040 and BU-0041 cite `source.locator: "AGENTS.md L150-153"`, but their stored `quote` field (verbatim, hash-verified against itself: sha256(quote)==quote_hash) is the 8-line paragraph actually spanning AGENTS.md L150–157, not L150–153. Re-opening only the cited 4-line span (L150-153) recovers less than half of what the record actually quotes — the quote is real and contiguous in the file (verified: it exists verbatim at L150-157), so this is not fabricated content, but the locator itself fails evidence-policy.md's own bar ("Precise enough for a human to re-open the exact evidence ... 'Somewhere in the file' is not a locator") by pointing at only half the actual cited span.
evidence: AGENTS.md lines 150-153 (`sed -n '150,153p'`) contain only the first half of the quote ("Every dispatched implementation ... skips the redundant no-mistakes"); the quote's remaining four lines ("`review` and `document` stages. Remediation that ... must not trigger repeated no-mistakes review cycles.") sit at lines 154-157, confirmed by `grep -n "skips the redundant no-mistakes" AGENTS.md` (line 155) and `grep -n "Every dispatched implementation" AGENTS.md` (line 150). Recomputed sha256 over the stored `quote` field's raw bytes exactly equals the stored `quote_hash` (`sha256:0ee3b567c9871d73d4269717ec77331bdb392791cb43b2b1b58d061981b5c18d`) for both records, confirming the quote text itself is genuine and internally hash-consistent — only the locator's line range is wrong.
